newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks push higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks push higher at close.

text.p: Powered by banks, Argentina's bolsa closed with a new moderate bounce Monday and looked set to stretch gains Tuesday, dealers said.

"Today the market showed special strength," said Luis Enrique Alvarez at brokers Alvarez. "Up until recently it looked firm but in need of a pause, but it seems to have consolidated over the weekend."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.4 percent to 587.60, stretching gains so far in November to 3.0 percent.
Traders noted volume rose despite the U.S. Veterans Day holiday, which drained strength from the local bonds market.

"Banks rose today on good results and also because their bond holdings have done very nicely," said Alvarez, referring to recent gains in government bonds on the back of the rallying U.S. Treasury market, which last week saw yields fall to an eight-month low of 6.51 percent.
The bolsa's three blue-chip banks, Bansud, Galicia and Frances, jumped 6.4 percent, 3.6 percent and 3.2 percent in the session, respectively.
"The bank sector usually spearheads trends, and the fact it rebounded today bodes very well for the market near-term," said dealer Emilio Alessandro.
The broad market index rose 1.3 percent, with winners smashing losers 36 to nine and 22 stocks closing unchanged.

"It's not just (falling international bond) yields but also local talk of a possible cabinet reshuffle which is cheering investors," said Alvarez. The media has speculated in recent days over possible changes of ministers, with only Economy Minister Roque Fernandez believed guaranteed to keep his post.
Floor volume swelled to 17.3 million pesos from Friday's dismal tally of 12.8 million, but over-the-counter turnover was extremely weak at 21.7 million against 63 million Friday.

The day's best main-tier performers besides banks were steelmaker Acindar and holding company Comercial del Plata, up 4.3 percent and 3.9 percent, respectively. Biggest losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa and petrochemical concern Indupa, off 1.9 percent and 1.5 percent each.
